fact: For any positive real s, if H^s_δ(E)≤H^(s+1)_δ(F) for every positive real δ, then H^s(E)≤H^(s+1)(F). This is indexed-supremum monotonicity on [0,∞].

grounds.reason: N005 supplies the pointwise inequality for every δ>0 whenever s>0.
D003 defines each Hausdorff measure as the supremum of these same contents over all positive real scales, with values in the extended nonnegative reals.
The current branch fixes 0<s<D, so both s and s+1 are positive; both suprema have the same index set.

justification: The probed theorem iSup_mono quantifies over a complete lattice and a common arbitrary index sort. Set its codomain to extended nonnegative reals, index to {δ:ℝ // 0<δ}, f(δ)=H^s_δ(E), and g(δ)=H^(s+1)_δ(F). The standard extended-nonnegative-real complete order supplies the lattice structure; N005 is exactly its only inequality premise. Unfolding D003 gives the displayed inequality. This is a basic order step, not a convergence or limit-interchange theorem.

fact: For x0∈Eucl(n) and real t,u, the coordinate-appending map e(t)=(x0,t) satisfies dist(e(t),e(u))=|t−u|. The basic real identity used to simplify the displayed metric formula is sqrt(a^2)=|a| for every real a.

grounds.reason: D001 supplies the Euclidean coordinate distance and the product-distance formula, including n=0.
H001 legitimately supplies a point x0∈E⊆Eucl(n).
The local map is defined by e(t)=(x0,t) with real interval domain I.
The formula is asserted for every t,u∈I, hence t,u are real numbers.

justification: Real.sqrt_sq_eq_abs has no hypotheses beyond a real argument. In D001's finite coordinate sum for dist(x0,x0), all summands vanish; the probed identity at a=0 gives sqrt(0)=0. Substituting this in the product metric leaves sqrt(|t−u|^2), which the same identity evaluates to ||t−u||=|t−u|. Absolute-value nonnegativity and idempotence are routine ordered-field case calculations. This verifies the actual displayed equality and its zero-dimensional case without importing any embedding or dimension theorem; the dimension theorem remains direct input N006.

fact: For finite real D>0 and a finite nonnegative real value d<D+1, there exists a real s with 0<s<D and d<s+1. Thus bounds dim_H(F)≥s+1 for every 0<s<D imply dim_H(F)≥D+1, also when dim_H(F)=∞.

grounds.reason: The branch assumes D>0, establishes the bounds for every 0<s<D, and explicitly considers dim_H(F)<D+1.
dim_H(F) lies in [0,∞]; under the strict comparison with finite D+1 it is a finite nonnegative real value.

justification: In the contradiction case write d for the finite real value of dim_H(F). Set s=D/2 if d≤1, and s=(D+d−1)/2 if d>1. In the first case 0<s<D and d−1≤0<s; in the second 0<d−1<D, so d−1<s<D. Both choices contradict d≥s+1. If dim_H(F)=∞ the desired lower bound already holds. This only checks the author's existing elementary choice and contradiction argument; no analytic limiting theorem, new assumption, or altered proof route is introduced.
